purpose: Fix 8 security/privacy audit findings (shell injection, credential exposure, temp file leaks, non-atomic writes, weak path validation, duplicated sanitization logic) across lib, action, and config packages.
riskRationale: Core security fixes (shell injection via execFileSync, shared sanitizeString utility, atomic JSON writes, path.relative() guard, askpass cleanup) are correctly implemented. However, 2 important issues remain from prior iterations: symlink bypass in the path traversal guard and incomplete Bearer token regex (missing Base64 padding, false positives from /gi flag).

text: The PR correctly addresses all 8 stated audit findings with clean, well-scoped changes. The CRITICAL shell injection fix (execFileSync for taskkill), consolidated sanitizeString utility eliminating code duplication, atomic write-to-temp-then-rename in JSON-DB, path.relative() guard against path normalization attacks, and askpass cleanup are all properly implemented. However, 6 previously-reported issues remain unaddressed: 2 important (symlink bypass in path traversal guard, Bearer token regex gaps) and 4 minor (missing JSDoc, stale .tmp cleanup, single askPassDir tracking, overly broad DB URI regex).

reasoning: 2 important and 4 minor issues from prior review iterations remain unaddressed. All have straightforward one-line fixes with no architectural impact. The core security fixes are correct and the PR makes meaningful improvements.

message: Correctly replaced cp.execSync with cp.execFileSync argument array for taskkill, eliminating the shell injection vector — the most critical fix in the PR.
Consolidated duplicate sanitization logic from logger.ts and action/src/utils.ts into a single shared utility, ensuring consistent credential redaction across all log/output channels.
Write-to-temp-then-rename pattern in both flushSync() and writeToDisk() provides atomic file persistence, preventing data corruption on crash.
Using path.relative() instead of startsWith for the directory check properly handles path-normalization attacks (e.g., /home/user-evil no longer bypasses the trusted-directory check).
Added process.on('exit') cleanup for askpass temp directories and removed chmodSync 0o755 overrides, preserving 0o700 restrictive permissions from writeFileSync.
Removed the PRIVATE_KEY inline field and updated the comment to discourage pasting secrets directly into .env files.

path.resolve(cfg) does not resolve symlinks. A git config --show-origin entry containing a symlink (e.g., .gitconfig symlinked to /etc/passwd) would bypass the path.relative() guard, as path.resolve only normalizes '.' and '..' but does not follow symlinks.
suggestion: Replace path.resolve(cfg) with fs.realpathSync(cfg) to resolve symlinks before the path traversal check. Wrap in a try-catch with a path.resolve fallback for safety against non-existent paths.

message: Bearer token regex has two issues: (1) character class [a-zA-Z0-9._\-+/]+ does not include '=', so standard Base64 padding characters leak past redaction; (2) /gi flag matches lowercase 'bearer ' in prose text, causing false positive redactions.
suggestion: Add '=' to the character class for Base64 padding coverage and drop the 'i' flag — the HTTP Authorization header is standardized as case-sensitive 'Bearer'.

message: sanitizeString is exported as a public API from lib/src/index.ts but has no JSDoc documenting what token patterns it redacts or when to use it.
suggestion: Add JSDoc describing the function, the token patterns it redacts (GitHub tokens, OpenAI keys, Anthropic keys, Slack tokens, Bearer tokens, env-var patterns), and its intended usage context (log/error sanitization).

message: The load() method does not clean up stale .tmp files from previous crashes. If the process crashes between writeFileSync(tmpPath) and renameSync(tmpPath, filePath), orphaned .tmp files accumulate on disk across restarts.
suggestion: Clean up stale .tmp files at the start of the load() method by checking for and removing any existing .tmp file associated with the target path before reading.

message: The process.on('exit') handler only cleans up the last assigned askPassDir. If configureGit() is called multiple times (e.g., different tokens in different webhook event handlers), earlier temp directories are orphaned until process exit. The 'exit' event also does not fire on SIGKILL.
suggestion: Consider adding SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that invoke cleanup, and either track all created directories in an array or reuse the existing askPassDir on subsequent calls.

message: The regex [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]+:// matches any URI scheme including file://. An error message containing file:///path/@something would incorrectly redact the path portion. Benign in practice (DB errors rarely contain file:// URIs) but could confuse debugging.
suggestion: Narrow the regex to only match known DB connection schemes (postgres://, mysql://, mongodb://) to eliminate false positives on file:// URIs.
